title: Conveyor belt early micro-tear defect detection
original_idea: Explore whether a combination of vibration and acoustic measurements can help identify an early mechanical defect in a conveyor-belt test setup before visible tear occurs.
problem: Early mechanical degradation and micro-tears in moving conveyor belts are visually imperceptible until catastrophic tearing occurs.
target_user: Industrial maintenance engineers and maker testbed operators.
environment: Benchtop conveyor test rig with acoustic motor noise and roller vibration.
mechanism: Localized micro-defects generate high-frequency acoustic emission bursts (>20 kHz) and transient vibration spikes when passing over rollers.
outcome: A reproducible detection threshold that distinguishes defect-induced signals from normal roller speed variations.
known_unknowns: Whether acoustic burst amplitude is overwhelmed by motor bearing noise
Whether vibration spikes vary primarily with roller RPM rather than defect presence
system_boundary: Benchtop conveyor rig, accelerometer, contact acoustic sensor, and data logging DAQ.
clarifying_questions: What is the maximum operating speed intended for the first test?
Is sensor mounting constrained to idler roller bearings?
